# Testing

## 12. Testing

Program settings have focused tests in `program_setting_test.dart`, `program_path_test.dart` and `program_box_test.dart`. They prove machine-only storage, defaults refused, executable discovery on a fixture PATH, explicit acceptance and typed paths, and the stored path's executable warning at 1200 and 700 pixels in light and dark themes.

The same manifest and consent tests prove the process capability's boolean declaration and one consent line per program. `plugin_log_test.dart` proves that each process door refuses a missing capability before dispatch, logging its full arguments.

`process_door_test.dart` runs a local Dart line-protocol fixture. It proves unchanged arguments containing spaces and `&` on Linux, stable default and explicit working directories, queued whole stdout and separately logged stderr, exit mid-receive, ownership refusal and release, cancellable waits, group cleanup including a child, and host survival across fresh JavaScript calls with disable, setting-change and exit cleanup. Its named Windows test, “Windows cmd path and argument with spaces”, proves a shim path and argument containing spaces on Windows; it is skipped on other systems. `engine_test.dart` proves all five frozen `ctx.process` doors across the real bridge. The process fixture also proves preservation of a concurrent setting edit while a program ignores TERM, and cancellation after a root exits while its child holds inherited pipes. `lifecycle_test.dart` proves process cleanup for failed Off, On and Allow writes, and `host_runtime_test.dart` proves it for a hung call.

The program-turn cases in `assistant_action_test.dart` run the same native fixture through a test text provider. They cover Stop while receiving, Stop between a tool answer's settlement and dispatch, failed and stale calls, a third repeated tool refusal, finalization, absent or throwing interrupts and their ordinary wall. They prove one fresh handover ledger, usage settled once, owner release, a surviving program after successful interruption and explicit fresh starts after failed cleanup. `dev_run_test.dart` proves both developer completion modes omit the wall despite their `dev.complete` recording label. `contract_test.dart` proves root operations are present and nested completions carry their calling frame id. It also proves done and failed frame owners are stopped, and a cancelled nested completion in another provider stops the caller-frame owner, discards queued output and lets the next operation start afresh. A one-shot fault in the existing process-stop wait proves that cleanup errors in both turn paths are logged and leave the backend free. A filtered ten-minute clock advances eleven minutes while a native program receive waits: completion remains pending with no wall timer, then Stop completes its handover. `run_offer_test.dart` checks that three nested completions each log a null wall with `reason: complete` and elapsed milliseconds. The fixture opens an existing key-backed Usage chain through the HTTP stand-in; native-route funding and admission remain the route's integration work.

### The universal core and the milestone suite

The **universal core** is the handful of end-to-end cases every change is proved against, whatever it touched: a project created, opened, edited through the autosave, saved, forked and picked; resolution (`pickAt`); the writer's refusals of a stale file and of another author's; a render through a stand-in backend; the command registry's dispatch; the whole app pumped once (`pumpApp`); the plans `010` and `020`; and the acceptance walk at 1200 × 800. It lives in one list, `scripts/test_core.txt`, each entry with a comment naming its case. A list has one entry per line, `#` comments and blank lines ignored: a test file's path from the root, a whole package (`packages/filmopen_format`), a plan (`plan:010`) or a walk's size (`walk:1200x800`).

A **milestone suite** is the core plus a chosen list of what the change could affect; the full suite runs at the major intersections only, such as a release candidate. The same selection drives every runner:

- `scripts/test_all.sh --core`, `--tests FILE` (repeatable) and `--full` — the default with no argument — and `scripts/test_all.ps1 -Core`, `-Tests FILE,…` and `-Full`. A selection runs each chosen package in its folder with the named files, or whole, and the root's files under the root's `flutter test`; a bad entry ends the run before anything runs, exit 2, naming the list, the line's number and a code (`bad-entry`, `no-such-test`, `no-test-folder`) — never the line's text, which could hold anything a caller pasted. Plans and walks in a list are ignored there. `scripts/test_all.ps1` also runs the repository's own Python tests in every mode, after the selection is checked and before the packages — `python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p test_*.py -v`, named with its folder and the `python` found, ending `test_all: done scripts/tests` with its elapsed time and exit code — and a failure there fails the run whatever the later suites do; no `python` on `PATH` is refused (`test_all: refused scripts/tests reason: no python on PATH`, exit 1). On Windows the tests that run a Linux-only script (`scripts/gate.sh`, `scripts/agent-run.sh`, `scripts/agent-vps.sh`) skip, naming it, and the rest need `bash` and `cmake` on `PATH` (MSYS2's `usr\bin` and `ucrt64\bin`, after the Windows Python).
- `scripts/gate.sh` runs `dart run scripts/gen_field_maps.dart --check` among its checks, whatever the selection (`scripts/tests/test_gen_field_maps.py`: every type written with its record and its change view, LF, its lines on stderr from start to the elapsed time; `--check` passing on a fresh file and leaving its bytes, failing on a stale one naming the difference and on a missing one, writing nothing; an unknown argument and `--out` without a file each refused with 64, a check of a file that is no UTF-8 and a write that cannot be made each failing with 1, every one logged from its start to `done:` with its code and milliseconds; writing over a file that is no UTF-8 replacing it and saying it changed; `test_gate_script.py`: a failing check failing the gate with its code). It requires one of `--full`, `--core`, `--tests FILE` or `--no-suite`, passes it to `test_all.sh`, adds the lists' `walk:` entries to its `--walk` sizes, and names it in its summary (`selection: core + list.txt`, `selection: none (checks only)`). It never runs a plan.
- `python3 test_plans/run_mcp.py --core` and `--tests FILE` run the lists' `plan:` entries, and `--plan` takes a comma-separated list; a selection keeps the runner's own order and its project handoffs. A list's `plan:130` is `test_plans/run_report.py`'s and is not run there. A wait for idle not met is said — `idle wait not met:` with the last tap or step, the answer and its seconds — and counted, never a failure: the common app's summary and each separate plan print their count, and the exit status stays the checks' failures. A tap that opens a menu waits for no idle, which the driver does not meet while a menu is open, and says so; the plan then taps its item (`scripts/tests/test_run_mcp_dispatch.py`).

`python3 scripts/select_tests.py <git range>` proposes the chosen list from the files a range changed: every changed package with a `test/` folder whole; every workspace package that depends on a changed one, directly or through others, whole, naming the changed package it reaches — the graph read from the pubspecs' `dependencies`, and their `dev_dependencies` too, since a test breaks when its fixtures' package changes; every root test file when the application depends on a changed package, else the root test files whose row in the table below names a changed root file (every root test file when no row does); and `plan:NNN` for a changed plan. A dependent without a `test/` folder is a comment line, as a changed one is. The root's own `pubspec.yaml` and `pubspec.lock` are not followed. It is a starting point to edit, not a rule, and says so on its first line. A range git refuses, or one shaped like an option, is refused (`bad-range`), as is a testing specification it cannot read when the table's rows are needed — a changed root file and no changed package the application depends on (`no-spec`).

The close smoke plan `test_plans/040_media.md` covers media through the UI and MCP control, at 1280 × 720 and at 700 × 800: every kind uploaded into the place a person chose — a clip refused by a picture place and taken by a character's *Motion clips*, always shown — each checked on the file's `media` container, the batch item's `n` and `group` and the folder, every `media:` identifier on the page naming its place, and the tile's provenance strip read through `find`; a picture place's refusal of a clip read as the sentence it says; a favourite, a move, an archive and its undoing, and a delete whose take's file and thumbnail, seen before, go, each read back from the file. The runner works in English, the one language shown, since it chooses a menu's items by their labels. Its places check retains identifiers read before scrolling and reaches *Motion clips*, the card's last place, before checking the five places' Upload and no *Add a place…*; a location's three places, no voice and no *Add a place…*. Its §10 case leaves and returns to a page during an import held by a loopback server, checks the place's own job tile, its *Stop* and its disabled *Upload*, then completion, and verifies one take, one batch and one entry with intervening typing retained.

The close smoke plan `test_plans/050_keys-dictation-usage.md` covers the speech keys on the two speech providers' pages — `fo-openai` and `fo-xai`, planted in a development folder, which every speech step needs — and a development-folder plug-in's own key on its page, inline dictation and Usage with fake credentials and scripted speech. It observes the default service before a missing-key failure replaces its tooltip, then chooses OpenAI and Grok explicitly and checks their models, setting events and separate totals. The actual message's *Open <provider>* action is discovered and pressed immediately, and lands on the provider's page. Summary is a prose box: while listening it shows the words provisionally, with no caption, and its file keeps the committed baseline; the second press commits the text once, and page departure cancels and restores the exact baseline. Each attempt requires its own new terminal event and expected file outcome, rather than a delay or an earlier attempt's event. Usage is zero only when its explicit empty sentence is present and its row controls are absent; accepted sessions require the populated controls and new Done rows with their file, minutes and cost. Light and dark captures show the provisional words and blue microphone, while selected service text withheld from agent values is checked on the pictures. The timestamped hold and keyboard rules remain widget-test and desktop-walk checks; the scripted agent does not prove hardware or live-service behavior.

The mutable document-copy regression also runs against the web runtime: from `packages/filmopen_format`, run `dart test --platform chrome test/json_document_test.dart`. It exercises clearing/refilling a decoded draft and the typed iteration used by the form after attachment.

The acceptance walk (`scripts/agent_walk.py`) waits for each event an act logs — an import's `media.imported`, Compare's durable `compare.copied`, a save, a fork, a player's release — from a log mark taken before the act, over the app's whole 500-event ring, so neither an earlier event nor a burst after it (save, refresh and sync events can follow before the tap answers) decides the step; every wait the walk polls prints its start (an event wait its mark and the events it reads, a timed wait its bound), its outcome and the time it took, and a refused log read is named in its failure line. A walk line masks only a VM service URL's auth code. It reaches a fork's exact child within `page.tree` before checking the row and its file. Plan `020_character-location.md` scrolls the page body up to Compare's heading before whole-copy, then retains its file assertion that copying does not remove the left version's other values.

The template is the plug-ins repository's: a suite that reads it (`filmopen_plugins`, `filmopen_plugin_host`, the root) needs the staged bundle, `plugins/stock.json`, which `scripts/test_all.*` and the gate stage first.

A replay has a 20-minute cooperative deadline that closes only its owned server input and permits the ordinary cleanup; expiry fails with status 124. The numbered runner bounds its replay child to 22 minutes, retaining partial stdout, stderr and status on timeout. Before cleanup, failed input is copied in full; a retention-copy failure is itself a failed check and keeps the original task home available rather than deleting the only input.

Where a test lives: with the code it proves — `dart test` in the pure packages, `flutter test` inside a Flutter package — unless it pumps the whole application, in which case it stays in the root `test/`; `scripts/test_all.sh` (or `test_all.ps1`) with no argument runs every suite. The gate on a Linux box is `scripts/gate.sh`: under one `flock` per box (`FILMOPEN_GATE_LOCK`, by default `/tmp/filmopen-gate.lock`), so that two gates never run their suites at once, it runs `flutter pub get`, `flutter analyze`, `scripts/check_document_keys.py` (zero offences), `scripts/package_digest.py` with the package pages then clean in `git status`, the scripts' unit tests (`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`), `scripts/test_all.sh` with the selection it is given — `--full`, `--core` or `--tests FILE`, one of which, or `--no-suite` to skip the suites, is required — and, once per `--walk WxH` and per `walk:` size of the selection's lists not given already, the agent walk on Linux with an empty keys folder and no `Xvfb` or `flutter run` left after it; each command's output goes to its own file under `--log` (by default a new folder under `~/gate-logs/`; a folder that already holds a run's evidence is refused, and nothing is written before the lock is held), a lock `flock` could not take runs no check, a `git status` that fails is not clean pages, a leftover process is logged by its pid and executable name only, and `scripts/gate_summary.py` ends the run with every command's exit code, the suites' counts read from each suite's terminal record — a suite without one fails by name — the selection, and `gate: PASS` or `gate: FAIL`; each command's elapsed seconds are on the console. Widget tests load projects in `setUpAll` because file IO does not complete inside a widget test's fake-async zone. Tree rows draw label and detail as one rich text; match them with `find.text('label detail', findRichText: true)`.

`flutter analyze` and `flutter test` must both be clean before a commit. Tests that need `dart:io` import the `_io` file directly (`log_file_io.dart`), because the analyzer resolves a conditional export to its stub.

The sync restart suite preserves closed-film checkpoints; the state adapter tests distinguish an open film without a target from closed/loading/other films without consulting its target. Payload and target tests verify bounded opaque payload identities and canonical folder hashing; target-transition tests separately pin hashed payload identities and the original identities retained in place keys.

Drive authentication lifecycle regressions in `drive_auth_test.dart` hold credential writes and refresh replies across cancellation, sign-out and a newer sign-in. The account tests prove a stale sign-in cannot overwrite the current signed-in hint.

The assistant suites run the host's fixture catalog package and test-only provider adapters in native QuickJS, with invented credentials and HTTP stand-ins. They cover the catalog's choices and offers, the opening's context and bounds, each turn's one bounded call and its Usage settled once, cancellation, staleness, the finalizer's proposal, and logs that carry the text as it is and never the stored key; `assistant_retained_test.dart` holds the final payload to the catalogue's output bound and one POST on the selected model and endpoint, writes a provider's lines and missing strings under an assistant binding, and proves Apply's fork of another author's version in use. The four catalog, action, retained and voice-action harnesses normalize fixture-relative separators to forward slashes on every platform. They establish protocol behavior rather than live model quality or speech conversation support.

The voice suites exercise both exact realtime configurations, streamed PCM, device-position truncation, late events, device and transport errors, pending-start and pending-stop cleanup, deduplicated Usage and a cap given to a session without real credentials. Live-caption cases cover cumulative corrections, fragment appends, final-text protection and retained incomplete text. WebRTC cases instead prove one direct multipart signaling request with initial turn detection disabled, the configured semantic VAD and far-field noise filter with PCM/Grok settings preserved, turn diagnostics that carry the person's words, the answer and the provider's error whole and drop unknown events, preservation of early data-channel events, native mute and End, integrated caption identities, no PCM or second socket, and speaking state independent of generation completion. Failed signaling closes the peer without retry or exposing provider error text. Pricing fixtures cover exact modality/cache rates, missing and contradictory usage, session-time versus cleanup time and outstanding responses. Widget cases exercise each caption state at 700 px in light and dark themes. The agent build's assistant fixture alone redirects application folders and reopens an absolute Windows preference filename, with `MemoryCredentialStore` and `StubKeyVerifier`; the product uses normal application state and native device credentials. The standalone Windows Media Foundation test (`test_native/synopsis_voice_audio/README.md` gives its commands) converts synthetic 44.1 kHz and 48 kHz stereo WAV files into 24 kHz mono PCM and checks frame count, frequency, amplitude and invalid input. Those checks do not establish live microphone, speaker, provider access or conversational quality. Only a person's Start gesture in the product on a device can perform that acceptance.

Native desktop probes and physical microphone, speaker and cleanup acceptance complement fixture tests; a generated SDP offer does not establish capture or audible playback.

The browser landing tests also pin a supplied parent id moving to its picked author while showing an older picked stem, an exact pinned scene, comparison-pair preservation, single-author project root highlighting, initial project-version landing, and a read-only chooser's exact session choice without a commentary write. Navigation log assertions retain the requested node and resolved stem/node, reason and elapsed time. A whole single-epoch character still exposes New outfit.

The project-page warning tests mount the actual detail pane, check the initially folded complete count and diagnostic text on a read-only project version, the zero-warning message, and the empty-folder diagnostics landing. They assert the fold gesture's state, full diagnostic text and elapsed time, and retain narrow light/dark layout checks.

The numbered project and character plans assert that a sole author leaves no author children under the project or epoch, then navigate to an exact older or newer stem for the existing fork, official, pick and comparison checks. The outfit plan reaches New outfit through the whole-character epoch overview. Desktop and drawer acceptance walks cover the same tree and project landing.
